jobs.description: TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. The position offers the chance to obtain further academic qualification (usually PhD).Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials, and their properties depend strongly on crystal structure. This project studies how atomic defects and strain affect the formation of magnetic domains and domain walls in altermagnetic single crystals such as MnTe and Fe2O3. The work combines advanced electron microscopy with magnetic imaging techniques. Within the SPP 2558 “Unconventional Magnetism: Beyond the S-Wave Magnetism Paradigm” and in strong collaboration with the group of Prof. Claire Donnelly (ETH Zürich), the successful candidate will help build a comprehensive picture of how structure and magnetism interact across different length. Tasks: - acquire and analyze aberration-corrected HR-(S)TEM images and determine local chemical compositions using EDS and EELS- perform large-field-of-view strain measurements with 4D-STEM and correlate strain and defect maps with XMCD imaging- develop and apply STEM-EMCD and vortex-EMCD techniques and apply them to altermagnets- collaborate with a PhD student of Prof. Claire Donnelly (Co-PI, responsible for XMCD)- publish and present results in peer-reviewed journals and at (inter)national conferencesRequirements: - a very good university degree (e. g. jobs.description: PhD position (m/f/d) in 4D Printing of Biodegradable Parts by Multi-Ink Binder Jetting (MultiMAM-101309938, DC-15)reference number 191/2026 is to be filled from 01.07.2027 or later.Pay grade: E13 TV-L Hours: 1.0 FTE (40 h/week)Contract type: limited to 36 monthsTechnical University Bergakademie Freiberg (TUBAF), Chair of Additive Manufacturing, invites applications for a fully funded PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network MultiMAM (Multi-Material Additive Manufacturing).About MultiMAM ProjectMultiMAM (project no: 101309938) is a European Doctoral Network dedicated to accelerating the industrial adoption of Multi-Material Additive Manufacturing (MMAM), a key enabling technology for next-generation healthcare, aerospace, automotive, energy, electronics, and multifunctional products. Bringing together leading universities, research institutes, and industrial partners from 10 European countries, MultiMAM addresses critical scientific and technological challenges across the MMAM value chain through 15 pioneering doctoral projects focusing on materials, processes, and sustainability.As a Doctoral Candidate in MultiMAM, you will benefit from world-class scientific training, international collaboration, interdisciplinary supervision, and industry-focused secondments. Working within a highly diverse and interdisciplinary network, you will develop advanced technical expertise, practical research experience, and transferable skills while contributing to innovative solutions for sustainable digital manufacturing. Upon completion, you will be well positioned to become a future leader in MMAM, advanced manufacturing, and industrial innovation.About MultiMAM Doctoral Candidate Project 15 (DC15): Binder Jetting (BJT) is an AM technology that uses liquid binders to join powder particles. This PhD project aims to develop sustainable alternatives to conventional materials by upcycling biobased waste for BJT. A key focus is the integration of multiple functional inks to create components with locally tailored properties, such as embedded electrical wiring, magnetic sensing and responsive behaviour. Furthermore, 4D printing will be explored to enable components to change their properties in response to external stimuli, such as temperature or moisture. The overall goal is to combine sustainable materials, functional integration and circular economy principles to develop adaptive components with self-repairing capabilities and controlled end-of-life disintegration.Research focus and responsibilities:• Implement BJT using upcycled, bio-based materials from renewable resources.• Apply functional inks with electrical, magnetic and responsive properties for externally triggered and fixed-time biocompatible degradation. These inks will be optimized for BJT printing parameters.• Advance BJT through the integration of 2-4 distinct inks and produce printed parts with multiple ink functionalities.• Contribute to project deliverables, scientific publications, dissemination, network-wide events, and collaboration across the MultiMAM doctoral networkProposed Doctoral Supervision Panel:Prof. Henning Zeidler, TUBAF, Germany, Dr. Katja Heise, TUBAF, GermanyProf. Rocco Lupoi, Trinity College Dublin, IrelandIndustrial Secondment (4 months) at C-MARX GmbH, Chemnitz, Germany.Academic Secondment (2 months) at Trinity College Dublin, Ireland.QualificationsApplicants must have:- A two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree in in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or a closely related discipline.- Excellent academic achievements and strong analytical and problem-solving skills.- Excellent English communication skills, both written and oral.- Interest in interdisciplinary research and international collaboration, and interest in getting science applied in industriesApplicants with experience in one or more of the following topics will be preferred:- Additive manufacturing, mechanical engineering, or machine design.- Process engineering and biobased material knowledge- Knowledge of stimuli-responsive materials.- Experimental work involving mechanical, optical, or chemical setups.- CAD modelling, mechanical design, or design optimisation.- Programming, automation, machine learning or real-time process control.- Thermal management, experimental design, or statistical data analysis.Approval and Enrolment Enrolment for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval by the faculty board. The candidate will be enrolled in the PhD degree programme (“Promotionsstudium”) at TUBAF. AssessmentThe assessment of the applicants will be made by the Doctoral Supervision Panel led by Prof. Henning Zeidler. Eligibility Requirements: Applicants must: - not already hold a doctoral degree, and fulfil the requirements for enrolment in TUBAF’s PhD programme. - comply with Marie Curie Mobility Rule: At the recruitment date, applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Germany for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before recruitmentFor the MultiMAM Doctoral Network project, a total of 15 PhD positions are available within the consortium. Applicants may apply for a maximum of two positions and must clearly indicate their first and second choices in each of the applications.Worrking Conditions, Benefits and Career DevelopmentThe successful candidate will be employed for 36 months as a research scientist within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network project at TUBAF. Starting date is 1st of July, 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.Working at the Resource University - regionally based and internationally networked. TU Bergakademie Freiberg is the university of resources and at the same time the oldest university of mining sciences in the world. Since its foundation in 1765, teaching and research have been oriented along the entire raw materials value chain. Today, this includes handling of natural raw materials from exploration, extraction, preparation and processing to recycling. The scientific fields represented at the university, which are reflected in the core fields of geo, materials, energy, environment and economics, are interlinked along the entire raw material value chain. The idea of sustainability, which was coined more than 300 years ago by Freiberg's chief miner Hans Carl von Carlowitz, was then as now the guiding principle in education and research.
